A web page as a block result

Source: R/html-page.R
html_page.Rd

html_page() returns an object that draws as a sandboxed iframe. A script block that ends with it shows the page on its card. Give it either html, a page you write, or url, a page that lives elsewhere.

Usage

html_page(
  html = NULL,
  url = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  height = "auto",
  sandbox = NULL,
  max_rows = 1000L,
  js_data = TRUE
)

Arguments

html

A mustache template, a single string or a character vector of lines.

url

A URL, with optional {name} placeholders.

data

A data frame, a list or a vector the page reads. NULL for none.

...

Further named values for the template or the URL. In a template the names rows, nrow and ncol are taken.

height

Height of the frame: a number of pixels or a CSS length such as "400px" or "50vh". "auto" fits an html page to its content; a URL page cannot be measured and defaults to "600px".

sandbox

The iframe's sandbox attribute, a single string. NULL takes the default for the mode.

max_rows

Rows of data passed to the page. More are dropped with a warning. Inf for no limit.

js_data

Whether scripts in the page get the data as blockr.data. With FALSE it is null.

Value

An object of class html_page.

HTML

html is a mustache template, filled in R with whisker. The template sees rows (one entry per row of data), nrow, ncol and any value passed in .... Use {{col}} for an escaped value and {{{col}}} for raw HTML. The escaping covers <, >, & and ", but not ', so write attributes with double quotes: <a title="{{col}}">.

Mustache cannot read a name that holds a dot or a space: it takes {{Sepal.Length}} for Length inside Sepal. The template therefore also gets each such column under a safe name, with dots and spaces replaced by underscores: {{Sepal_Length}}. A template that writes the real name gets a warning.

Scripts in the page read the same data as JSON from blockr.data, an array of row objects with the real column names, or null without data. Missing values differ between the two: the template writes NA, Inf and NaN as text, and blockr.data holds null. Date-times are written in UTC ("2026-01-02T03:04:05Z").

The data travels to the browser with the page, once in the filled template and once in blockr.data, and again each time the block re-renders. max_rows limits it. A page that only uses the template can set js_data = FALSE to leave blockr.data out, which about halves the size. rows is only built when the template uses it.

The page runs in an iframe with sandbox = "allow-scripts": its CSS and JS cannot reach the board. The sandbox does not keep the page from sending its data to other hosts. A script, an image or a style sheet in the page can load from anywhere and pass along what the page holds. With height = "auto" the iframe grows to fit the page, up to 20000 pixels.

URL

{name} in url is filled from the first row of data, or from a value in ..., and URL-encoded. The filled URL has to start with http:// or https://. The other site has to allow framing: a site that sends X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN, or a CSP frame-ancestors that does not list the board's host, stays blank. A link above the frame opens the page in a new tab.

The frame keeps allow-same-origin, because an external app needs its own cookies and storage. The sandbox therefore only protects the board from pages on another host. A URL on the board's own host can reach the board and everything the viewer can do on it.

Outside a board

At the console, printing the object opens the page in the viewer. In a script run with Rscript it prints one line. In an R Markdown or Quarto document with HTML output the frame is part of the document.

Examples

html_page("<h1>{{title}}</h1>", title = "Hello")
#> <html_page> html, 671 characters, height auto

html_page(
  "<ul>{{#rows}}<li>{{name}}: {{band}}</li>{{/rows}}</ul>",
  data = data.frame(name = c("Mick", "John"), band = c("Stones", "Beatles"))
)
#> <html_page> html, 771 characters, height auto

html_page(url = "https://example.org/search?q={q}", q = "blockr")
#> <html_page> https://example.org/search?q=blockr, height 600px
